title: Coding Set 05: Anagram Equivalence & Circular Rotation
description: Reported string/array coding problems: case-insensitive anagram check ignoring spaces and in-place right rotation by K.

problems.title: Anagram Check Ignoring Case & Spaces
problems.statement: Given two strings S1 and S2 on separate lines, determine whether S1 and S2 are anagrams of each other after ignoring all whitespace characters and letter casing (case-insensitive). Print 'ANAGRAM' if they are, otherwise 'NOT ANAGRAM'.
problems.inputFormat:
Line 1: String S1.
Line 2: String S2.
constraints: Strings contain ASCII letters, digits, and spaces

starterCode.python:
import sys

s1 = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip('\r\n')
s2 = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip('\r\n')
# Write your solution here

solutions.python:
import sys
from collections import Counter

s1 = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip('\r\n')
s2 = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip('\r\n')
c1 = Counter(ch.lower() for ch in s1 if not ch.isspace())
c2 = Counter(ch.lower() for ch in s2 if not ch.isspace())
print('ANAGRAM' if c1 == c2 else 'NOT ANAGRAM')

edgeCases: Strings with differing whitespace counts ('Dormitory' vs 'Dirty room')
Punctuation differences ('!' is non-whitespace, must mismatch)

problems.title: Rotate Array Right by K Positions
problems.statement: Given an integer array A of size N and a non-negative integer K, rotate the array to the right by K steps in-place (using O(1) extra space) and print the resulting array.
problems.inputFormat:
Line 1: Two integers N and K.
Line 2: N space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: N space-separated integers after rotating right by K.

starterCode.python:
import sys

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n, k = data[0], data[1]
a = data[2:2+n]
# Write your solution here

solutions.python:
import sys

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n, k = data[0], data[1] % data[0]
a = data[2:2+n]
if k:
    a = a[-k:] + a[:-k]
print(' '.join(map(str, a)))

edgeCases: K > N (must reduce K %= N, and K can be 10^9 so read as long)
